extracted.intended_audience: Prospective applicants to the Paul & Daisy Soros Fellowships for New Americans (immigrants and children of immigrants applying to graduate/professional school)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and evaluation-related requirements for applying to the Paul & Daisy Soros Fellowships for New Americans, including eligibility, required materials, essay prompts and limits, recommendations, submission rules, and selection timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Our eligibility requirements include your status as an immigrant or a child of immigrants, your age, and your academic standing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We do not look at school, GPA, or test score range for eligibility. All eligibility requirements should apply to you as of the deadline. If named a finalist, you will be required to provide documentation of your eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supported degree types and timing to apply
rubrics_metrics.description: PD Soros supports all types of full-time graduate and professional degrees at accredited institutions in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can apply when you’re applying to graduate or professional school, or when you’re in the first two years of the academic program you’re seeking funding for.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required application components
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must create an account and submit an online application including demographic and eligibility questions, educational history, the graduate program(s) for which funding is sought, transcripts, a resume/CV, two essays, and register three to five recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All application materials must be submitted online through the online application. Optional exhibits are accepted. The first year of the Fellowship can’t be deferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essay One prompt and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell us about your experiences as a New American. Whether as an immigrant yourself, or as a child of immigrants, how have your experiences as a New American informed and shaped who you are and your accomplishments?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feel free to discuss how individual people (such as family or teachers), institutions, aspects of law, culture, society or American governance made an impact on your life as an immigrant or child of immigrants. The program is interested in understanding the context of your personal, professional, and academic accomplishments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essay Two prompt and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell us about your current and near-term career-related activities and goals, as well as why you decided to pursue the specific graduate program(s) and school(s) that you have.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how you see your current work and study informing your early career goals. If you have not been accepted into a program yet, tell us why you selected the programs to which you are applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essay word limits and submission format
rubrics_metrics.description: Each essay has a maximum length of 1,000 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a hard limit. You’ll have to copy and paste your essays into a text box.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resume/CV length and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no page limit for resumes & CVs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resumes are typically 1-2 pages but we see all lengths of resumes and CVs. The application will preserve formatting, since it will convert uploaded and filled in fields into PDF format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardized test score requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Only upload the test scores that were required for admission to the graduate program you want the Fellowship to fund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your program requires only MCAT, upload MCAT; if only GRE, upload GRE. If you will take a required exam after the deadline, select the option indicating you will take it later and upload scores when available. If your program requires multiple exams, you can upload the scores you have and a note that you will take the other exam on X date and will send scores later.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to upload test scores
rubrics_metrics.description: Upload the examinee score report or a screenshot of your online account where scores are posted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If selected as a finalist, you will be asked to provide an official score report. Do not type up your scores in a Word document and self-report them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcript requirements for application
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit an image of your transcript that includes your name and the institution’s name; unofficial transcripts are sufficient for the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are selected as a finalist we will request your official transcript.

rubrics_metrics.name: GPA reporting for nonstandard systems
rubrics_metrics.description: If your university does not use a typical Grade Point Average (GPA) system, how to report GPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write “0.00” in the space provided if your undergraduate or graduate program does not use a typical GPA system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendations: count and required submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must register three to five recommenders; a minimum of three recommendations must be submitted by the application deadline for the application to be considered complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations must be submitted online through the application system. You can submit your application before your recommendations have been submitted, but your application will be incomplete unless at least three recommendations are received by the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendations: registration and identity verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Each recommender must be registered separately so we can verify their identities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommenders will receive an email from a smapply.io address with instructions; applicants should verify they clicked 'save' after registering each recommender. If recommenders don’t receive emails, check junk mail and use 'Resend Invitation' once. The system requires separate registered recommenders even if a letter is multi-signed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-signed recommendation letters
rubrics_metrics.description: A recommendation letter signed by more than one person counts as one recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application system still requires three to five separately registered recommenders; a multi-signed letter can be uploaded by one recommender but the applicant still needs additional registered recommenders to reach the minimum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation content guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters of recommendation should educate and contextualize the achievements and choices of each applicant for the screeners and panelists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full guidance for recommenders is provided via a link; applicants can find guidance on who to select as a recommender. There is no page or word limit for recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline strictness
rubrics_metrics.description: Application and recommender deadlines are strictly enforced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All application materials must be submitted by 2 pm ET on the deadline date. The program makes no exceptions to the 2 pm ET application deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method
rubrics_metrics.description: All application materials must be submitted online through the online application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We do not accept any materials by mail or e-mail. Any hard copies received will not be included or returned. Interfolio instructions are the applicant's responsibility; we recommend submitting directly via our system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Returning applicants policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for applicants who applied in prior cycles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You will not be able to resubmit your previous application. You must upload your resume, essays, transcripts, standardized test scores and optional test scores through the current application system. Recommendations from prior years cannot be forwarded to the current application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling password-protected PDFs
rubrics_metrics.description: If a PDF (e.g., GRE report) is password-protected and cannot be uploaded, how to proceed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the party who provided the PDF to remove security. If not possible, print the pages, then scan the printed pages into a valid file format and upload the new document. Configure the scan output to standard US Letter size (8 x 11 in).

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional exhibits
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may include optional exhibits with their application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fellowship has minimized official documents required to confirm eligibility, educational, and test results; optional exhibits are accepted but finalists will be asked for specific official documents if advanced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection process and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: After review, the top 77 applicants will be designated finalists and asked to appear for virtual interviews; 30 of the 77 finalists will be selected as Fellows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications due Oct 29, finalists notified mid-January, interviews late Jan/early Feb, winners notified in March, Fellows announced publicly in April, Fellowship support and Fall Conference begin in the following academic year. Exact dates are provided per cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finalist documentation and interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: If named a finalist, you will be required to provide documentation of your eligibility and other official documents, and participate in virtual interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program will specify the official documents needed from finalists before inviting them to interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application cost and reapplication
rubrics_metrics.description: Application is free and applicants may apply more than once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The first year of the Fellowship cannot be deferred. Apply again if appropriate, but follow returning applicant rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advice on essay reuse
rubrics_metrics.description: You may use essays previously written for graduate school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether a previous essay best answers the PD Soros question and conveys what you most want to share; adapt as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical support and help-desk hours
rubrics_metrics.description: Where to go for help with uploading or application system issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SurveyMonkey (SMApply) help desk for uploading issues (available Monday–Friday 8 am–8 pm ET). PD Soros staff are available Monday–Friday 9 am–5 pm ET for Fellowship-specific questions.
